title: Introduce provenance score and weighted ingest to correct console per-model share after late imports
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Large, late ingestion batches (manual imports, customer-provided replays, and occasional ledger repairs) are skewing per-model percentage breakdowns in the Console. The current charts treat all events as equal regardless of provenance, which causes transient false spikes and long tails after backfills. Impact is incorrect billing-attribution perception, confusing SRE/Customers, and noisy alerts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console per-model breakdowns expose a new provenance filter (real-time vs backfill vs repaired) and default to a weighted view that de-emphasizes non-real-time events. 2) Provenance score computed per event is stored alongside existing telemetry with no schema breaking changes. 3) Historical charts can be toggled between raw-count, weighted, and provenance-filtered views. 4) No measurable increase in query latency for dashboards (+ < 50ms p95) and storage delta < 5% for added fields. 5) Rollout plan and migration executed with a staging replay validating behavior for three representative customers.
design_notes: We will assign a lightweight provenance_score (0.0-1.0) to events when ingesting: real-time events default to 1.0, identified backfill batches get 0.2-0.6 depending on age and declared batch flag, and repaired/ledger-replay events get 0.1. The score is multiplicative with token/embedding counts for aggregation. Rationale: preserve visibility of backfills while reducing their influence on normalized shares. We must persist provenance metadata as a single nvarchar column 'prov_tag' and a float 'prov_score' in the event store to avoid complex schema migrations.
tradeoffs: - Pros: preserves raw telemetry while preventing late-batch noise in normalized charts; easy UI filtering; small storage increase. - Cons: introduces heuristic parameters (score buckets) that may need tuning; customers might be surprised if UI defaults differ from raw counts; requires careful migration/backfill when re-evaluating historical rows.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Ingest tagging (2w) - add prov_tag/prov_score at producer level (edge-ingest & batch-replay pipeline). Phase B: Aggregation change (2w) - update OLAP rollups to compute both raw_sum and weighted_sum. Phase C: Console UX (1w) - add toggle and provenance legend. Phase D: Staging validation & customer replays (1w) - run synthetic replays across staging customers and compare with baseline. Phase E: Canary rollout to 5% tenants then full rollout with opt-out for 48h. Total ~6 weeks.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for prov_score math and edge cases. - Integration tests with streaming pipeline to ensure tags survive shard merges and replays. - Synthetic-stress job simulating a 24h late-import of 10% of tokens for three tenant archetypes. - Dashboard smoke tests verifying weighted vs raw deltas and ensuring p95 query latency < baseline + 50ms.
qa_checklist: 1) Confirm prov_tag set for manual import jobs. 2) Confirm provenance_score preserved through retries and dedupe. 3) Validate console toggles show expected numbers against prepared replay ground truth. 4) Validate no regression in billing exports (billing CSV must still reflect raw token counts). 5) Run incident simulation where a repaired run is ingested; ensure alerts do not fire at current thresholds due to weighted view.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy ingest tagging behind feature flag. 2) After 24h of metrics stability, enable weighted aggregation in analytics backend for staging. 3) Run two-day synthetic replay validation. 4) Canaries: enable for 5% of tenants, monitor per-model churn and alert rate for 72h. 5) Full enable with announcement and UI education doc. 6) Provide opt-out API for tenants who want raw view default.
monitoring_and_observability: We will add these monitors: prov_tag_ingest_rate (expected ~100% of ingest sources annotated within 1h), weighted_vs_raw_ratio_alert (if divergence > 30% for >2h for >10 tenants), dashboard_query_latency_p95, and an anomaly dashboard showing top 20 models where provenance-weighting changed rank. Add an audit log of feature flag flips and tenant opt-outs.
migration_notes: For historical rows we will not rewrite existing event stores initially. Instead, the analytics rollup job will backfill weighted aggregates for the last 30 days in a controlled backfill window using staged compute to avoid peak load. If customers request older re-computation, create a ticket to run a targeted re-aggregation job per tenant.
